title: Enterprise model fallback: cost & latency sensitivity study and compatibility matrix
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run a structured market research and competitive analysis to produce an enterprise-facing compatibility matrix and sensitivity study that maps alternative open and commercial LLMs to Redwood deployment constraints (latency, unit cost, quantization/OPS compat, licensing, regional availability). Outcome will inform automated fallback rules and procurement recommendations for Dedicated/Private offerings.
acceptance_criteria: CSV compatibility matrix with at least 30 candidate models and 12 columns (token_limit, FLOPS_profile, best_known_quant, throughput on p4, inference_cost_estimate, license_type, regional_availability, observed_latency_95, known-degrading-prompt-patterns, eval_quality_score, security_flags, vendor_stability)
Heatmap visualizing tradeoff surfaces (cost vs latency vs quality) for three representative enterprise workloads: high-throughput embeddings, low-latency chat, and long-context summarization
Documented fallback policy templates (canary -> compatible-quantized -> lower-quality with price cap) and a recommended priority order for automated routing
Signal integration checklist and alerting rules for model break/failover triggers in Console (e.g., latency spike > 2x baseline, quality regression > 4% on benchmark prompts)
Stakeholder sign-off from Product, Research, and Sales on procurement recommendations
methodology: Primary signals: vendor release notes, model card metadata, benchmark results from in-house eval harness, community telemetry (OSS forks, quantization reports)
Benchmarks: run three synthetic workloads across chosen models and hardware (p4, a10g, t4) to gather latency_50/90/95 and tokens/sec
Cost model: combine instance unit cost, measured tokens/sec, and batching assumptions to produce per-1k-token cost estimates
Qualitative inputs: interviews with 6 enterprise customers on fallback tolerance and desired guarantees
Licensing/legal scan: flag models with unclear commercial terms or copyleft clauses
